Question: I'm using STM32F429 with SDRAM and LCD. After some time the display shows corrupted pixels. I tried increasing FMC timings but it doesn't help.
Answer: Check AHB bus matrix arbitration between LTDC and FMC/DMA. LTDC has high bandwidth demand and competes with DMA for SDRAM access. Increase LTDC line buffer watermark, reduce SDRAM burst length, or use dedicated SRAM for framebuffer layer. Also verify SDRAM refresh timing is not violated during LTDC active display period.

Question: HAL_UART_Receive_DMA works fine for the first transfer but after calling it a second time nothing is received. Using STM32F446RE Nucleo.
Answer: After a DMA transfer completes, the UART state machine remains in HAL_UART_STATE_BUSY_RX. Call HAL_UART_DMAStop() or HAL_UART_Abort() before re-initiating. Alternatively check that RxXferCount is reset and DMA stream is properly re-enabled with correct NDTR value.

Question: I get a HardFault when I enable FreeRTOS on my F407 project. Stack seems fine. It crashes in vTaskStartScheduler. CubeMX generated code.
Answer: The SVC_Handler in stm32f4xx_it.c conflicts with FreeRTOS port handler. CubeMX should route SVC_Handler to FreeRTOS but if you have a manual stm32f4xx_it.c it may override it. Remove or weak-link SVC_Handler and PendSV_Handler in your IT file. Also verify configPRIO_BITS matches your NVIC (4 for Cortex-M4).

Question: USB CDC on STM32F411 sometimes stops enumerating after host sleep/wake cycle. Need to unplug and replug. Is this a known issue?
Answer: After host suspend, the USB peripheral may miss the resume signaling. Enable remote wakeup capability, handle SUSPEND/RESUME callbacks in usbd_conf.c, and ensure USB clock (48MHz from PLL) is re-stabilized before responding. On F411, verify OTG_FS_GCCFG NOVBUSSENS bit if VBUS detection is not wired.

Question: SPI with external flash W25Q128 works at 1MHz but fails at higher speeds on STM32F401. CubeMX project. What could cause this?
Answer: GPIO speed must match SPI clock. For SPI > 10MHz set GPIO to Very High speed in CubeMX. Also check: CPOL/CPHA match W25Q128 requirements (Mode 0 or Mode 3), adequate decoupling on flash VCC, and proper chip select timing (tCSH between commands).

Question: I2C on my STM32F446 randomly hangs. The busy flag stays set and nothing recovers it except a full reset. Is there a workaround?
Answer: This is a known silicon limitation on F4 I2C (analog filter glitch). Workaround: disable analog filter (HAL_I2CEx_ConfigAnalogFilter with DISABLE), implement bus recovery by toggling SCL as GPIO 9 times to release SDA, then re-init I2C. Some users also add external pull-up resistors (2.2K instead of 4.7K).

Question: STM32F407 ETH stops receiving after a few hours. LWIP stats show memory errors. CubeMX 6.x generated.
Answer: ETH DMA RX descriptors run out because LWIP pbufs are not freed properly. Check that low_level_input() returns pbuf to pool, increase PBUF_POOL_SIZE, and verify ETH_RXBUFNB matches. Also in ethernetif.c ensure HAL_ETH_GetReceivedFrame_IT handles all pending frames in a loop, not just one per interrupt.

Question: CAN on STM32F405 works in loopback but not in normal mode. Checked termination and baud rate.
Answer: Common causes: (1) GPIO AF not set correctly for CAN TX/RX pins, (2) CAN transceiver standby pin left floating or high, (3) missing 120 ohm termination on BOTH ends of bus. Also verify CAN bit timing: check BTR register prescaler and segment values match the physical bus clock. Use CAN analyzer to confirm TX frame is actually driven on the wire.

Question: ADC DMA continuous mode on F446: values correct then suddenly all read 0 or 4095. Custom board.
Answer: ADC overrun occurs when DMA cannot keep up. Enable OVR interrupt to detect it. Use circular DMA mode and ensure DMA buffer size matches number of converted channels. If multi-channel scan, verify regular sequence length in SQR registers. Also check analog supply (VDDA) is stable and reference voltage is not drooping under load.

Question: PWM on TIM1 CH1 (STM32F411) glitches when I update CCR1. How to avoid?
Answer: Enable preload on CCR1 (TIM_CCMR1_OC1PE bit) so the new value takes effect only at next update event. Also set ARPE in TIM_CR1 for auto-reload preload. Update CCR1 anytime; it will be loaded into shadow register at UEV. If using center-aligned mode, be aware of double-update behavior.

Question: After updating STM32CubeF4 package, my F429 project doesn't compile. Error in stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.h.
Answer: Check CubeF4 release notes for breaking changes. Common issue: macro renames like __HAL_RCC_GET_SYSCLK_SOURCE() or struct field renames in RCC_OscInitTypeDef. Pin your project to a specific FW version in CubeMX (Project Manager > Firmware Package) or update your code to match new macro names documented in release notes.

Question: How to configure MPU on STM32F4 to avoid DMA cache coherency issues? I get stale data.
Answer: On F4 (Cortex-M4 without cache), this issue is less common. If using F7 HAL on F4 project by mistake, remove cache ops. For F4 the real issue is usually DMA reading from CCM-RAM which is not DMA-accessible. Ensure DMA buffers are in SRAM1/SRAM2. Use linker attributes to place DMA buffers: __attribute__((section('.dma_buffer'))).

Question: STM32F469 Discovery LCD example works but adding my code turns screen white.
Answer: Likely heap/stack overflow corrupting LTDC framebuffer. LTDC uses large framebuffer in SDRAM. If your code also allocates from heap in SDRAM, overlap occurs. Check linker script to separate framebuffer region from heap. Also verify PLLSAI clock for LTDC is not disturbed by your clock reconfiguration.

Question: FDCAN on STM32H563 receives frames but timestamp is always zero. Enabled timestamp in CubeMX.
Answer: FDCAN timestamp counter needs explicit enable: set TSCC.TSS bits to select internal counter and configure TSCC.TCP prescaler. CubeMX may generate init code but the counter start requires FDCAN_EnableTimestampCounter() call after HAL_FDCAN_Start(). Also verify message RAM configuration includes timestamp element in RX FIFO element size.

Question: Trying TrustZone on STM32H573, debugger disconnects as soon as I enable it.
Answer: Enabling TZEN option byte restricts debug access. Before setting TZEN: (1) configure secure debug authentication in option bytes, (2) ensure your ST-Link firmware supports secure debug, (3) program SECWM and SAU before enabling TZEN. To recover: use STM32CubeProgrammer with hot-plug under reset, or regression to RDP level 0 if RDP is not at level 2.

Question: OSPI memory-mapped mode works but indirect write is very slow on STM32H5.
Answer: In indirect mode, each write waits for FIFO threshold + busy flag. Optimize: increase FIFO threshold level, use DMA for indirect writes instead of polling, enable write-back caching on the region if doing many small writes. Also check OSPI clock divider - higher clock = faster write cycles.

Question: ICACHE enabled on H563 causes random crashes. Disabling fixes it. Silicon bug?
Answer: Not a silicon bug in most cases. If your code modifies flash content (bootloader, OTA) or uses memory-mapped OSPI that changes, you must invalidate ICACHE after updates. Call HAL_ICACHE_Invalidate() after any flash/OSPI write. Also check MPU attributes: if non-cacheable region overlaps cacheable, behavior is unpredictable.

Question: Trying to boot from external OSPI flash on STM32H5. Bootloader starts but app doesn't execute.
Answer: Configure option bytes: set BOOT_ADDR to OSPI memory-mapped address (0x90000000). Ensure OSPI is initialized by system bootloader or your first-stage loader before jumping. The MCU cannot auto-configure OSPI at boot unless using boot-from-OSPI mechanism. Verify vector table is correctly placed at mapped address.

Question: USB HS internal PHY on H5 not enumerated on Windows. Works on Linux. CDC class.
Answer: Windows is stricter on USB descriptor timing and compliance. Check: (1) device descriptor bcdUSB should be 0x0200 for HS, (2) configuration descriptor wTotalLength is exact, (3) string descriptors use proper LANGID. Also verify HS PHY calibration trim values. Try connecting through a USB2.0 hub to isolate HS negotiation issues.

Question: STOP2 current on H563 is 50uA, datasheet says ~5uA. All GPIO set to analog.
Answer: Common culprits: (1) SWD pins still connected to debugger (remove probe), (2) LSE bypass mode without crystal draws current, (3) some peripherals not fully gated - check RCC_AHB/APB_SMENR for unwanted clocks in stop, (4) voltage scaling not set to lowest range before stop entry, (5) SRAM retention enabled for unused banks.

Question: GPDMA linked-list mode on H5 only executes first node then stops. No error flag.
Answer: Check CLLR register in first node: it must contain the address of next node structure (word-aligned). Common mistake: CLLR points to start of next node but offset must account for the specific register update mask. Verify node structures are in non-cacheable SRAM or cache is invalidated. Also ensure GPDMA channel is configured for linked-list mode (not single block).

Question: RNG returns HAL_ERROR after waking from STOP on H5.
Answer: RNG needs PLL or HSI48 clock which is stopped in STOP mode. After wakeup, re-enable RNG clock source and call HAL_RNG_Init() to re-condition the entropy source. The CONDRST (conditioning reset) bit must be set then cleared. Add this sequence in your wakeup callback before calling HAL_RNG_GenerateRandomNumber().

Question: ThreadX on H5: tx_thread_sleep doesn't enter low power, just busy-waits.
Answer: ThreadX requires you to implement tx_low_power_enter() and tx_low_power_exit() hooks. By default these are empty stubs. Implement WFI/STOP entry in tx_low_power_enter, clock restoration in tx_low_power_exit, and configure LPTIM as ThreadX timer source for tickless operation. See STM32Cube ThreadX LowPower example.

Question: Secure FW update on H5: wrote image to non-secure bank, swap doesn't happen on reset.
Answer: Bank swap requires: (1) set SWAP_BANK bit in FLASH_OPTCR via option byte programming (not just flash write), (2) perform OB launch (HAL_FLASH_OB_Launch), (3) system reset. Verify you're using the correct flash bank mapping and that BFB2 option bit is configured. The swap is physical remapping, not just logical.

Question: STM32H573I-DK demo hangs on splash screen. Flashed binary from CubeFW package.
Answer: Board revision mismatch. Newer H573I-DK boards (rev C) may need updated BSP that handles LCD controller differences. Check board silkscreen revision vs CubeFW release notes. Also verify external OSPI flash is not empty if demo reads assets from it. Try the demo source project instead of pre-built binary.

Question: LPUART on STM32U575 loses first byte waking from STOP2. Wakeup on start bit, LSE clock.
Answer: LSE-clocked LPUART needs time to recover after STOP2 exit. The start bit wakeup triggers clock restoration but first byte is partially received during recovery. Workaround: use address match wakeup mode and send a dummy preamble byte, or switch to HSI kernel clock with STOPWUCK for faster wakeup at cost of power.

Question: B-U585I-IOT02A WiFi stopped working after firmware update. EMW3080 unresponsive.
Answer: The EMW3080 module has its own firmware that must match the STM32 driver version. If you updated CubeU5 package but not EMW3080 FW, communication protocol may be incompatible. Reflash EMW3080 with matching version from en.x-wifi-emw3080b.zip package. Check UART baud rate between STM32 and module hasn't changed.

Question: TouchSensing on U5 works at room temp but unreliable above 50°C. Nucleo-U575.
Answer: TSC charge transfer measurement drifts with temperature due to parasitic capacitance changes. Implement dynamic threshold recalibration: periodically re-measure reference channel and adjust detection thresholds. Also increase acquisition cycles (CTPH/CTPL), enable shield electrode to reduce environmental coupling.

Question: How to store encryption keys in OTP on STM32U5? HAL sequence unclear.
Answer: Sequence: (1) HAL_FLASH_Unlock(), (2) HAL_FLASH_OB_Unlock(), (3) write to OTP area using HAL_FLASH_Program() with FLASH_TYPEPROGRAM_QUADWORD at OTP base address (0x0BFA0000 on U5), (4) HAL_FLASH_OB_Lock(), HAL_FLASH_Lock(). OTP is one-time: test on non-critical area first. Lock bits prevent further writes per block.

Question: OCTOSPI HyperRAM read errors when burst crosses 1KB boundary on U5.
Answer: HyperRAM has row boundary at 1KB (device-dependent). Configure OSPI with correct device size and wrap mode. Set DEVSIZE correctly and enable boundary crossing handling in OSPI DCR1 register (MTYP=HyperBus). The HAL must split transactions at row boundaries or configure the RAM's burst wrap length to match.

Question: STM32U585 STOP3 current 10x higher than expected. All peripherals off.
Answer: Check: (1) PWR_CR1 SRAM retention bits - disable retention for unused SRAM banks, (2) SMPS vs LDO selection in STOP3 (SMPS is more efficient), (3) flash memory power-down in STOP3, (4) all I/Os truly in analog or output low (floating inputs leak), (5) measure without debugger connected, (6) check if RTC with LSE enabled adds expected quiescent current.

Question: ADF microphone on U5 DK gives noisy output. BSP audio example unmodified.
Answer: Check PDM clock frequency matches microphone datasheet (typically 1.2-3.2 MHz). ADF decimation ratio must produce correct audio sample rate. Common issue: clock polarity inversion causes half-period sampling errors. Verify CKBEN and CCK configuration in ADF_CKCFGRx. Also check microphone power supply filtering on the board.

Question: How to use PKA for ECDSA on STM32U5? Documentation minimal.
Answer: Use HAL_PKA_ECDSASign() with PKA_ECDSASignInTypeDef structure. Fill in: curve parameters (prime P, order N, generator G), private key, hash of message. Call HAL_PKA_Init(), HAL_PKA_ECDSASign() in blocking mode, then HAL_PKA_ECDSASign_GetResult() for (r,s). See Projects/NUCLEO-U575/Examples/PKA/PKA_ECDSASign for reference.

Question: LPBAM: LPTIM triggering ADC in STOP2 on U5, ADC never converts.
Answer: LPBAM autonomous mode requires: (1) ADC AMEN bit set in ADC_CR, (2) LPTIM configured with AMEN for autonomous trigger, (3) DMA channel in LPBAM mode linked to ADC, (4) correct trigger connection in LPTIM TRIGSEL. All three peripherals (LPTIM, ADC, DMA) must be in autonomous mode. Check CubeMX LPBAM configuration utility.

Question: DMA transfer error on U5 when src=SRAM4, dst=OCTOSPI. Works with SRAM1.
Answer: On STM32U5, SRAM4 is on a different AHB port than SRAM1. The GPDMA channel port assignment (SRC/DST port selection in channel config) must match the memory location. Configure DMA channel with correct source port for SRAM4 (check LPDMA vs GPDMA channel assignment matrix in reference manual).

Question: MDF output saturated even with low mic signal on U5. Gain adjusted.
Answer: Check OFSSET and SHIFT fields in MDF_DFLTxCR register. SHIFT reduces the output bit width and can cause clipping if too aggressive. Set SHIFT=0 initially, verify raw output, then incrementally shift. Also check if integrator mode (SITF) is enabled by mistake - it accumulates and saturates quickly.

Question: USB PD on U5 negotiates 5V but never requests higher voltage. CubeMX UCPD.
Answer: UCPD requests higher voltage by sending PD Request message after receiving Source_Capabilities. Check that your PD stack (STM32 USBPD middleware) has sink PDOs configured for higher voltages (9V, 15V, 20V). In CubeMX USBPD configuration, add requested PDOs in Sink PDO list. The PD policy engine must select an appropriate PDO from source's advertised list.

Question: Secure boot on U5: provisioned with TrustedPackageCreator, now bricked. No SWD.
Answer: If RDP is set to level 2, device is permanently locked. If RDP level 1: use STM32CubeProgrammer in hot-plug mode with NRST held, then perform RDP regression to level 0 (this erases all flash). If TZEN=1 with secure debug disabled, you need ECDSA authentication via DA (debug authentication) protocol. Contact ST support if DA keys are lost.

Question: SubGHz radio on WL55 transmits but receiver never gets packet. Two Nucleo-WL55JC.
Answer: Check: (1) both boards use same frequency, modulation, sync word, and preamble settings, (2) RF switch (FE_CTRL1/2/3 GPIO) is correctly configured for TX on sender and RX on receiver, (3) antenna is connected to correct port (LP/HP), (4) packet type matches (LoRa vs FSK). Run SubGHz_Phy_PingPong example first to validate hardware.

Question: LoRa P2P works at close range but fails beyond 100m. Expected km.
Answer: For maximum range: use SF12, BW125kHz, CR4/8. Check: (1) TX power set to maximum (+22dBm with PA boost on HP path), (2) correct antenna port selected (HP not LP), (3) antenna gain/orientation, (4) clear line of sight for test. Also verify TCXO startup time is sufficient and frequency error is within tolerance.

Question: STM32WL deep sleep 10uA instead of 2uA. Radio BUSY low confirmed.
Answer: After confirming radio is in sleep: (1) check SMPS configuration - SMPS must be in step-down mode for lowest power, (2) verify all GPIO are set to analog (especially unused RF pins), (3) disable debug (DBGMCU_CR=0), (4) check if HSE32 CSS is enabled (adds quiescent current), (5) measure on VBAT not VDD if RTC is powered separately.

Question: IPCC CM0+ to CM4 notification missed under high LoRaWAN traffic on WL.
Answer: IPCC miss happens when CM4 doesn't process channel fast enough and CM0+ overwrites. Implement proper flow control: CM0+ should wait for channel free flag before writing. Increase IPCC interrupt priority on CM4 side. If using Sequencer, ensure LoRaWAN task does not block IPCC processing task for too long.

Question: LoRaWAN OTAA join works on TTN but fails on Chirpstack. Same keys.
Answer: Key byte order issue: TTN displays DevEUI/AppKey in MSB format, Chirpstack may expect LSB or vice versa. Check JOIN_EUI (AppEUI) byte order too. Also verify: (1) Chirpstack RX2 parameters match (SF12/869.525MHz for EU868), (2) ADR settings don't conflict, (3) frequency plan on Chirpstack matches your channel configuration.

Question: How to implement FUOTA on STM32WL? No clear example in CubeWL.
Answer: CubeWL includes LoRaWAN Packages (clocksync, fragmentation, firmware management) in Middlewares/Third_Party/LoRaWAN/LmHandler/packages/. Enable LORAWAN_DATA_DISTRIB_MGT and LORAWAN_FRAG_DECODER flags. The FUOTA process requires: fragmentation transport, reassembly, signature verification, then bootloader jump. See AN5554 and STM32WL FUOTA application note.

Question: Sigfox certification fails on spectrum mask, TX looks clean on my analyzer.
Answer: Certification tests use very tight frequency/time resolution. Common issues: (1) PA ramp-up/down time too fast causes spectral splatter (adjust RADIO_RAMP_* settings), (2) modulation index not exactly matching Sigfox spec (BPSK ±100Hz deviation), (3) temperature drift during production test. Apply per-device frequency trimming and verify at temperature extremes.

Question: Radio IRQ on WL sometimes not triggered after TX. DIO1 stays low. Needs reset.
Answer: After TX complete, IRQ must be explicitly cleared by reading IRQ status register via SubGHz_ReadCommand(RADIO_GET_IRQSTATUS) then clearing with RADIO_CLR_IRQSTATUS. If your ISR doesn't clear all pending flags, next TX may not trigger IRQ. Also verify DIO1 mapping includes TxDone event (SetDioIrqParams). Check for race condition between SetTx and IRQ clear.

Question: Custom WL55 board + TCXO: +/-2kHz offset between units. Calibration doesn't fix.
Answer: Per-device trim is needed. Use SubGHz_SetXtalCap() or frequency offset calibration. Measure actual frequency with spectrum analyzer and apply trim in SubGHz_RadioSetXoscTrim(). Store trim value in flash/OTP per unit. Also verify TCXO supply voltage is stable and startup time (TCXO_CTRL_DELAY) is long enough for your crystal.

Question: Switch LoRa/FSK on WL without full radio reinit, is it possible?
Answer: Yes. Call SetPacketType(PACKET_TYPE_LORA) or SetPacketType(PACKET_TYPE_GFSK) followed by reconfiguring modulation/packet params. No need for full init. However, SetPacketType changes internal radio state, so you must call SetModulationParams and SetPacketParams again after switch. SetRfFrequency can remain if same frequency.

Question: Sigfox credentials provisioning on custom STM32WL board. Nucleo procedure doesn't apply.
Answer: For custom boards: (1) order Sigfox Device Kit (PAC+ID) from Sigfox buy portal, (2) program credentials into STM32WL secure storage (NVM or option bytes) using Sigfox Credential Management utility, (3) register device on Sigfox backend with PAC. The Nucleo uses pre-provisioned STS module which custom boards don't have. See Sigfox_PushButton example credentials section.

Question: WL LoRaWAN node stops sending after days. Radio stuck. Only reset works.
Answer: Implement radio watchdog: if no TxDone/RxDone within expected timeout, force radio reset via SubGHz_SetStandby() then full re-init. Common root cause: unhandled error state (RADIO_ERROR_TIMEOUT flag) leaving radio in undefined mode. Add Radio.Reset() in error callback and monitor BUSY pin as health check in main loop.
